hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Inverted Customer Return Spillover (pv13_custretsig_retsig, 22d Decay) (pv13)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Directly refines the breakthrough from Batch 169 Candidate 1 (which achieved Sharpe 1.11, Sub-universe 0.52, and 0.00 Self-Correlation with zero warnings, but was penalized by 28% turnover). By extending the linear decay horizon from 10 days to 22 trading days (1 calendar month), we smooth out transitory customer return noise. This compresses portfolio turnover from 28% down to ~12%-14%. Because Fitness scales inversely with the square root of turnover, this 50% turnover compression multiplies Fitness by ~1.41x, directly propelling Fitness into the 1.20-1.50 target zone while maintaining zero portfolio self-correlation.
confounders: Macroeconomic cyclical demand shifts lifting entire supply chain ecosystems simultaneously
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha underperforms if longer-horizon customer return shocks fail to reflect supplier margin recovery.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutral 22-day linearly decayed inverted customer return signal engineered for low turnover and high capital efficiency

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Inverted Customer Return 20d Moving Average (pv13_custretsig_retsig) (pv13)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Applies an unweighted 20-day rolling time-series mean (ts_mean) to inverted customer return signals (pv13_custretsig_retsig). Rolling moving averages exhibit significantly higher memory persistence and lower daily turnover than linear decay filters, reducing turnover into the 10%-12% sweet spot. This maximizes the platform capital efficiency metric (Fitness = Sharpe * sqrt(|Returns| / Turnover)) while harvesting the identical +1.11 to +1.48 Sharpe anomaly with 0.00 portfolio self-correlation.
confounders: Sudden discontinuous supply chain disruptions that render trailing 20-day averages stale
Broad market trend regimes overriding supplier-specific margin pressures
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha breaks down if equal-weighted 20-day customer returns lag price adjustments by more than 30 days.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutral 20-day moving average of inverted customer return signals delivering smooth, low-turnover execution

hypotheses.title: Options Contrarian Put/Call Open Interest Ratio 20d Decay (pcr_oi_30) (option9)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Exploits institutional hedging overreaction and contrarian options sentiment using 30-day put/call open interest ratios (pcr_oi_30, 98% coverage). When institutional investors panic, put option open interest surges relative to call open interest, driving pcr_oi_30 to elevated extremes. Conversely, low put/call open interest indicates complacency. Shorting equities with excessive put/call open interest (or going long low-pcr names) captures the relief rally as institutional hedges are rolled or unwound. Open interest updates daily and moves gradually, ensuring low portfolio turnover (< 12%) and zero correlation with accounting metrics.
confounders: Genuine existential distress where extreme put open interest correctly anticipates insolvency
Options market illiquidity during market closures
hypotheses.falsification_test: Alpha fails if elevated put/call open interest ratios consistently predict persistent subsequent equity underperformance.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutral 20-day decayed inverted put/call open interest ratio capturing institutional hedging exhaustion
